questions.stem: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard language used to create and structure content on the web using elements called tags.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag is used to define a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: <a> (anchor) is the HTML tag used to create hyperlinks. It wraps the clickable text or image and uses the href attribute to specify the destination URL.

questions.stem: Which attribute specifies the URL in an anchor tag?
questions.explanation: The href attribute (Hypertext Reference) in an anchor tag specifies the URL of the page the link goes to. It is the core attribute that makes a link functional.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag creates the largest heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> creates the largest and most important heading in HTML. Headings range from <h1> (largest) to <h6> (smallest), with <h1> typically used for main page titles.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag inserts a line break?
questions.explanation: is the HTML tag for a line break. It is a void element (self-closing) and forces the content after it to start on a new line.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag is used to insert an image?
questions.explanation: is the correct HTML tag for embedding images. It requires a src attribute for the image source and an alt attribute for accessibility.

questions.stem: What attribute of provides alternate text?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute of provides alternate text that is displayed if the image cannot be loaded and read by screen readers for accessibility.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag creates an unordered list?
questions.explanation: <ul> (unordered list) creates a bulleted list in HTML. Each item inside is wrapped in <li> tags. Unordered means the items have no specific sequence.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag creates an ordered list?
questions.explanation: <ol> (ordered list) creates a numbered list. Items inside are wrapped in <li> tags and are automatically numbered by the browser.

questions.stem: Which tag defines a list item?
questions.explanation: <li> (list item) defines each individual item within both <ul> (unordered) and <ol> (ordered) lists in HTML.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag defines a table row?
questions.explanation: <tr> (table row) defines a horizontal row inside an HTML table. It is always nested inside <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, or <tfoot>.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag defines a table header cell?
questions.explanation: <th> (table header) defines a header cell in a table. By default, content in <th> is bold and centered, distinguishing headers from data cells.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag defines a table data cell?
questions.explanation: <td> (table data) defines a standard data cell in an HTML table. It holds the actual content of the table and appears inside <tr> elements.

questions.stem: What attribute in <table> adds a border?
questions.explanation: The border attribute in a <table> tag adds a visible border around the table and its cells. In modern HTML, CSS is preferred, but the attribute still works.

questions.stem: What does the colspan attribute do in a table cell?
questions.explanation: The colspan attribute makes a table cell span across multiple columns. For example, colspan='2' makes one cell occupy the space of two columns.

questions.stem: What does the rowspan attribute do?
questions.explanation: The rowspan attribute makes a table cell span across multiple rows. For example, rowspan='3' makes one cell occupy the height of three rows.

questions.stem: Which tag is used to define an HTML form?
questions.explanation: <form> is the HTML tag used to create an interactive form. It wraps input elements and has action (where to send data) and method (GET or POST) attributes.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a text field?
questions.explanation: <input type='text'> creates a single-line text input field where users can type plain text such as a name or search query.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a password field?
questions.explanation: <input type='password'> creates a password field that masks the user's input with dots or asterisks for security purposes.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a submit button?
questions.explanation: <input type='submit'> creates a button that submits the form data to the server when clicked. It triggers the form's action attribute.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a reset button?
questions.explanation: <input type='reset'> creates a button that resets all form fields back to their initial/default values when clicked.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag creates a dropdown list?
questions.explanation: <select> creates a dropdown list in HTML. Users can choose one or more options from the list. Options are added using <option> tags inside it.

questions.stem: Which tag is used with <select> to add items?
questions.explanation: <option> tags are used inside <select> elements to define each selectable item in the dropdown list.

questions.stem: Which tag creates a multi-line text input?
questions.explanation: <textarea> creates a multi-line text input field. Unlike <input type='text'>, it allows users to enter multiple lines of text and can be resized.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a checkbox?
questions.explanation: <input type='checkbox'> creates a checkbox, which is a small square that users can check (select) or uncheck. Multiple checkboxes can be selected simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which input type creates a radio button?
questions.explanation: <input type='radio'> creates a radio button. Radio buttons are grouped by the same name attribute, allowing only one selection from the group at a time.

questions.stem: What does the 'action' attribute of a form specify?

questions.explanation: The action attribute of a <form> specifies the URL where form data is sent when the form is submitted. It defines the server-side script that processes the data.

questions.stem: What does the 'method' attribute of a form specify?
questions.explanation: The method attribute of a <form> specifies the HTTP method used to send form data — either GET (appended to URL) or POST (sent in request body).

questions.stem: Which HTML tag makes text bold?
questions.explanation: <b> makes text bold in HTML. While <strong> also makes text bold with semantic importance, <b> is purely presentational with no semantic meaning.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag makes text italic?
questions.explanation: <i> makes text italic in HTML. While <em> also italicizes with semantic emphasis, <i> is purely presentational styling.

questions.stem: What does the <head> tag contain?
questions.explanation: The <head> tag contains meta-information about the HTML document — such as the title, character set, CSS links, and JavaScript references — not visible content.

questions.stem: Which tag sets the page title shown in the browser tab?
questions.explanation: <title> sets the text shown in the browser tab and bookmarks. It also appears as the page title in search engine results.
